verses.1:1: There was a man in the land of Uz named Job, and that man was blameless and upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.
verses.1:2: And seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
verses.1:3: His livestock numbered seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys, along with a very great household of servants; so that this man was the greatest of all the people of the East.
verses.1:4: Now his sons would go and hold a feast in the house of each one on his own day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
verses.1:5: And it came to pass, when the days of feasting had completed their round, that Job would send and consecrate them; and he would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, "Perhaps my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." Thus Job did continually.
verses.1:6: Now there came a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them.
verses.1:7: And the LORD said to Satan, "From where do you come?" Then Satan answered the LORD and said, "From roaming across the earth, and from walking back and forth in it."
verses.1:8: Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil?"
verses.1:9: So Satan answered the LORD and said, "Does Job fear God for nothing?
verses.1:10: Have You not put a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that belongs to him on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have spread abroad in the land.
verses.1:11: Yet stretch out Your hand now and touch all that belongs to him, and surely he will curse You to Your face!"
verses.1:12: And the LORD said to Satan, "Behold, all that he has is in your hand; only upon him do not stretch out your hand." So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
verses.1:13: Now there came a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother.
verses.1:14: And a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the female donkeys were grazing beside them,
verses.1:15: when the Sabeans swept down and carried them off; and they struck down the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.1:16: While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The fire of God fell from heaven and burned among the sheep and the servants and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.1:17: While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three companies, raided the camels and carried them off, and struck down the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.1:18: While he was still speaking, yet another came and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,
verses.1:19: and behold, a mighty wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, so that it collapsed upon the young people, and they died; and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.1:20: Then Job arose, tore his robe, and shaved his head; and he fell to the ground and worshiped.
verses.1:21: And he said, "Naked I came forth from my mother's womb, and naked I shall return there. The LORD has given, and the LORD has taken away; may the name of the LORD be blessed."
verses.1:22: In all this Job did not sin, nor did he ascribe any wrong to God.
verses.2:1: Again there came a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
verses.2:2: And the LORD said to Satan, "From where have you come?" Then Satan answered the LORD and said, "From roaming across the earth, and from walking back and forth in it."
verses.2:3: Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil? Still he holds fast to his integrity, though you incited Me against him to destroy him without cause."
verses.2:4: Then Satan answered the LORD and said, "Skin for skin! Indeed, all that a man owns he will give for his life.
verses.2:5: Yet stretch out Your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh, and surely he will curse You to Your face!"
verses.2:6: And the LORD said to Satan, "Behold, he is in your hand; only spare his life."
verses.2:7: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with grievous boils from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head.
verses.2:8: And he took for himself a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself with, while he sat in the midst of the ashes.
verses.2:9: Then his wife said to him, "Do you still hold fast to your integrity? Curse God and die!"
verses.2:10: But he said to her, "You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we indeed accept good from God, and not accept adversity?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
verses.2:11: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this calamity that had come upon him, each one came from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite—for they had agreed together to come to grieve with him and to comfort him.
verses.2:12: And when they lifted up their eyes from afar and did not recognize him, they raised their voices and wept; each man tore his robe, and they threw dust toward heaven upon their heads.
verses.2:13: So they sat with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was exceedingly great.
verses.3:1: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
verses.3:3: "May the day perish on which I was born, and the night that declared, 'A male child is conceived.'
verses.3:4: May that day be darkness; may God above not seek after it, and may no light shine upon it.
verses.3:5: May darkness and the shadow of death claim it; may a thick cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day terrify it.
verses.3:6: As for that night, may thick gloom seize it; may it not rejoice among the days of the year; may it not enter into the number of the months.
verses.3:7: Behold, may that night be barren; may no sound of gladness enter into it.
verses.3:8: May those who curse the day denounce it, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.
verses.3:9: May the stars of its twilight grow dark; may it hope for light and find none, nor behold the eyelids of the dawn;
verses.3:10: because it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb, nor hide trouble from my eyes.
verses.3:11: Why did I not die at birth, and expire as I came forth from the womb?
verses.3:12: Why did knees receive me, and why were there breasts, that I should nurse?
verses.3:13: For by now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept, and then I would have found rest—
verses.3:14: with kings and counselors of the earth, who rebuilt ruins for themselves,
verses.3:15: or with princes who possessed gold, who filled their houses with silver;
verses.3:16: or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like infants who never saw the light?
verses.3:17: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary in strength find rest.
verses.3:18: Together the captives are at ease; they hear no voice of the taskmaster.
verses.3:19: The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
verses.3:20: Why is light given to one in misery, and life to those bitter of soul,
verses.3:21: who wait for death, yet it does not come, and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
verses.3:22: who rejoice with exultation and are glad when they find the grave—
verses.3:23: to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
verses.3:24: For my sighing comes before my bread, and my groanings pour out like water.
verses.3:25: For the dread that I feared has come upon me, and what I trembled at has befallen me.
verses.3:26: I am not at ease, nor am I quiet, nor do I have rest, yet turmoil has come."
verses.4:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.4:2: "If one ventures a word to you, will you grow weary? Yet who is able to withhold words?
verses.4:3: Behold, you have instructed many, and you have strengthened feeble hands.
verses.4:4: Your words have raised up the one who was stumbling, and you have made firm the buckling knees.
verses.4:5: But now it comes to you, and you grow weary; it reaches you, and you are dismayed.
verses.4:6: Is not your reverence your assurance, and the blamelessness of your ways your hope?
verses.4:7: Remember now: who, being innocent, has ever perished, and where have the upright been destroyed?
verses.4:8: As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble reap it.
verses.4:9: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His wrath they are consumed.
verses.4:10: The roar of the lion, and the cry of the fierce lion—the teeth of the young lions are broken out.
verses.4:11: The strong lion perishes for want of prey, and the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad.
verses.4:12: Now a word was stealthily brought to me, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
verses.4:13: Amid unsettling thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men,
verses.4:14: dread befell me, and trembling, which caused all my bones to shudder.
verses.4:15: Then a spirit glided past my face; the hair of my flesh stood on end.
verses.4:16: It stood still, yet I could not discern its appearance; a form was before my eyes. There was stillness, and I heard a voice:
verses.4:17: 'Can mortal man be righteous before God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?
verses.4:18: Behold, He does not put His trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error;
verses.4:19: how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation rests in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
verses.4:20: From morning to evening they are shattered; with no one taking notice, they perish forever.
verses.4:21: Is not their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and without wisdom.'"
verses.5:1: "Call now—is there anyone who will answer you? And to whom among the holy ones will you turn?
verses.5:2: For vexation slays the foolish man, and jealousy puts the simple one to death.
verses.5:3: I myself have seen a fool taking root, yet suddenly I cursed his habitation.
verses.5:4: His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate, and there is none to rescue them.
verses.5:5: His harvest the hungry devours, taking it even out of the thorns, and a snare pants after their wealth.
verses.5:6: For affliction does not come forth from the dust, nor does trouble sprout from the soil;
verses.5:7: but man is born for trouble, even as the sparks mount upward.
verses.5:8: Yet as for me, I would seek after God, and to God I would entrust my cause—
verses.5:9: who performs great things beyond searching out, and wondrous deeds without number.
verses.5:10: He gives rain upon the face of the earth, and sends waters across the open fields,
verses.5:11: to set the lowly on high, and those who mourn are raised up to deliverance.
verses.5:12: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.
verses.5:13: He ensnares the wise in their own craftiness, and the counsel of the wily is brought to a hasty end.
verses.5:14: By day they encounter darkness, and they grope at noonday as in the night.
verses.5:15: But He delivers the needy from the sword of their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.
verses.5:16: So there is hope for the poor, and injustice shuts its mouth.
verses.5:17: Behold, blessed is the man whom God reproves; so do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.
verses.5:18: For He inflicts pain, yet He binds up; He smites, yet His hands heal.
verses.5:19: In six troubles He will rescue you, and in seven no calamity shall touch you.
verses.5:20: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the grasp of the sword.
verses.5:21: From the lash of the tongue you shall be hidden, and you shall not fear devastation when it comes.
verses.5:22: At devastation and famine you shall laugh, and do not fear the wild beasts of the earth.
verses.5:23: For your covenant shall be with the stones of the field, and the wild beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.
verses.5:24: You shall know that your tent abides in peace; you shall inspect your habitation and miss nothing.
verses.5:25: You shall also know that your seed shall be numerous, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
verses.5:26: You shall come to the grave in full vigor, like a stack of grain brought in at its season.
verses.5:27: Behold, this we have searched out, and so it is; hear it, and know it for yourself."
verses.6:2: "Oh, that my vexation were surely weighed, and my calamity lifted together with it in the balances!
verses.6:3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; therefore my words have been rash.
verses.6:4: For the arrows of the Almighty are in me, and my spirit drinks their venom; the terrors of God marshal themselves against me.
verses.6:5: Does the wild donkey bray over green grass, or does the ox low over its fodder?
verses.6:6: Can that which is tasteless be eaten without salt, or is there any flavor in the white of an egg?
verses.6:7: My soul refuses to touch them; they are as loathsome food to me.
verses.6:8: Oh, that my petition might come to pass, and that God would grant what I long for:
verses.6:9: even that God would be pleased to crush me, that He would loose His hand and cut me off!
verses.6:10: Then this would still be my consolation—yes, I would exult in anguish though He does not spare—for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
verses.6:11: What is my strength, that I should still wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
verses.6:12: Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh made of bronze?
verses.6:13: Is it not so that there is no help within me, and that resourcefulness has been driven from me?
verses.6:14: To the despairing man, lovingkindness is due from his friend, even though he should forsake the fear of the Almighty.
verses.6:15: My brethren have dealt treacherously like a brook, like the channels of streams that pass away,
verses.6:16: which are darkened by reason of the ice, and in which the snow conceals itself.
verses.6:17: In the season when they grow warm, they vanish; when it is hot, they disappear from their place.
verses.6:18: The courses of their way turn aside; they go up into the wasteland and perish.
verses.6:19: The caravans of Tema looked; the companies of Sheba waited in hope for them.
verses.6:20: They were put to shame because they had been confident; they came there and were confounded.
verses.6:21: For now you have become as nothing; you behold terror and are afraid.
verses.6:22: Did I ever say, 'Give to me, or from your substance offer a bribe on my behalf,
verses.6:23: or deliver me from the hand of the adversary, or redeem me from the hand of the ruthless'?
verses.6:24: Teach me, and I will hold my peace; make me understand how I have erred.
verses.6:25: How forceful are upright words! Yet what does your reproving prove?
verses.6:26: Do you intend to reprove mere words, when the speeches of a despairing man are as wind?
verses.6:27: Indeed, you would even cast lots over the fatherless, and bargain over your friend.
verses.6:28: Now therefore, be pleased to look upon me; for surely I will not lie to your face.
verses.6:29: Turn now, let there be no injustice; yes, turn again, for my righteousness is still in this cause.
verses.6:30: Is there injustice upon my tongue? Cannot my palate discern calamity?"
verses.7:1: "Is there not an appointed hard service for mortal man upon the earth? Are not his days like the days of a hired laborer?
verses.7:2: Like a servant who pants for the shade, and like a hired laborer who eagerly awaits his wages,
verses.7:3: so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been appointed to me.
verses.7:4: When I lie down, I say, 'When shall I arise?' Yet the night stretches long, and I am filled with restless tossing until the dawn.
verses.7:5: My flesh is clothed with worms and crusts of dust; my skin hardens and breaks open afresh.
verses.7:6: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
verses.7:7: Remember that my life is but a breath; my eye will never again behold good.
verses.7:8: The eye of him who sees me shall gaze upon me no longer; Your eyes shall be upon me, and I shall be no more.
verses.7:9: As a cloud fades and passes away, so he who goes down to Sheol shall not ascend.
verses.7:10: He shall never return to his house, nor shall his place recognize him anymore.
verses.7:11: Indeed, I will not hold back my mouth; I will speak out in the distress of my spirit; I will utter my complaint in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.7:12: Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that You set a guard over me?
verses.7:13: When I say, 'My bed will comfort me, and my couch will bear away my complaint,'
verses.7:14: then You frighten me with dreams, and through visions You terrify me,
verses.7:15: so that my soul would choose strangling, and death rather than these bones of mine.
verses.7:16: I loathe my life; I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a mere breath.
verses.7:17: What is mortal man, that You should magnify him, and that You should set Your heart upon him,
verses.7:18: that You should visit him morning by morning, and test him moment by moment?
verses.7:19: How long will You not turn Your gaze from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow my saliva?
verses.7:20: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O Watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?
verses.7:21: Why then do You not forgive my transgression and cause my iniquity to pass away? For soon I shall lie down in the dust; You will search for me diligently, but I shall not be."
verses.8:1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.8:2: "How long will you speak these things, and the words of your mouth be like a mighty wind?
verses.8:3: Does God pervert justice, or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
verses.8:4: If your children have sinned against Him, He has delivered them into the hand of their transgression.
verses.8:5: If you will earnestly seek God and make supplication to the Almighty,
verses.8:6: if you are pure and upright, surely even now He would rouse Himself for you and restore the habitation of your righteousness.
verses.8:7: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would increase exceedingly.
verses.8:8: For inquire, please, of the former generation, and give heed to what their fathers have searched out;
verses.8:9: for we are but of yesterday and know nothing, because our days upon the earth are a shadow.
verses.8:10: Will they not teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their heart?
verses.8:11: Can the papyrus grow up without a marsh? Can the reed grass flourish without water?
verses.8:12: While it is still in its greenness and not cut down, it withers before any other grass.
verses.8:13: So are the paths of all who forget God, and the hope of the godless shall perish,
verses.8:14: whose confidence is broken off, and whose trust is a spider's web.
verses.8:15: He leans upon his house, but it will not stand; he holds fast to it, but it will not endure.
verses.8:16: He is fresh and green before the sun, and his shoots spread forth over his garden.
verses.8:17: His roots are entwined about the stone heap; he looks upon a place of stones.
verses.8:18: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, 'I have not seen you.'
verses.8:19: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the dust others shall spring forth.
verses.8:20: Behold, God will not cast away the blameless, nor will He uphold the hand of evildoers.
verses.8:21: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.
verses.8:22: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked shall be no more."
verses.9:2: "Truly I know that it is so; but how can a man be righteous before God?
verses.9:3: If one desired to contend with Him, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
verses.9:4: He is wise in heart and mighty in strength; who has hardened himself against Him and prospered?
verses.9:5: He removes the mountains, and they do not know it, when He overturns them in His wrath;
verses.9:6: He shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble;
verses.9:7: He commands the sun, and it does not rise, and He seals up the stars;
verses.9:8: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads upon the waves of the sea;
verses.9:9: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;
verses.9:10: He does great things beyond searching out, and marvelous things without number.
verses.9:11: Behold, He passes by me, and I do not see Him; He moves on, yet I do not perceive Him.
verses.9:12: Behold, if He snatches away, who can turn Him back? Who can say to Him, 'What are You doing?'
verses.9:13: God will not turn back His anger; beneath Him the helpers of Rahab bow low.
verses.9:14: How much less then can I answer Him, and choose out my words with Him?
verses.9:15: Though I were righteous, I could not answer; I would make supplication to my Judge.
verses.9:16: If I called and He answered me, I would not believe that He had given ear to my voice.
verses.9:17: For He crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause.
verses.9:18: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
verses.9:19: If it is a matter of strength, behold, He is mighty; and if of justice, who will appoint a time for me?
verses.9:20: Though I were righteous, my own mouth would condemn me; though I were blameless, it would prove me perverse.
verses.9:21: I am blameless; I have no regard for myself; I despise my life.
verses.9:22: It is all one; therefore I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.'
verses.9:23: If a scourge slays suddenly, He mocks at the trial of the innocent.
verses.9:24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covers the faces of its judges. If it is not He, who then could it be?
verses.9:25: Now my days are swifter than a runner; they flee away and see no good.
verses.9:26: They glide by like skiffs of reed, like an eagle swooping down upon its prey.
verses.9:27: If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad countenance and be of good cheer,'
verses.9:28: I dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not hold me innocent.
verses.9:29: I shall be accounted wicked; why then do I labor in vain?
verses.9:30: If I wash myself with snow water and cleanse my hands with lye,
verses.9:31: yet You will plunge me into the pit, and my own garments will abhor me.
verses.9:32: For He is not a man, as I am, that I should answer Him, and that we should come together in judgment.
verses.9:33: There is no arbiter between us, who might lay his hand upon us both.
verses.9:34: Let Him take His rod away from me, and let His dread not terrify me.
verses.9:35: Then I would speak and not fear Him; for it is not so with me."
verses.10:1: My soul abhors my life; I will let loose my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.10:2: I will say to God, "Do not condemn me; make known to me why You contend against me."
verses.10:3: Is it good to You that You should oppress, that You should reject the labor of Your hands, and shine forth upon the counsel of the wicked?
verses.10:4: Do You have eyes of flesh, or do You see as mortal man sees?
verses.10:5: Are Your days like the days of a mortal, or Your years like the days of a man,
verses.10:6: that You seek out my iniquity and search after my sin,
verses.10:7: though You know that I am not wicked, and there is none who can deliver out of Your hand?
verses.10:8: Your hands shaped me and fashioned me altogether round about, yet You destroy me.
verses.10:9: Remember, I pray, that You formed me like clay; and will You turn me back to dust?
verses.10:10: Have You not poured me out like milk, and congealed me like cheese?
verses.10:11: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and wove me together with bones and sinews.
verses.10:12: You have granted me life and lovingkindness, and Your watchful care has guarded my spirit.
verses.10:13: Yet these things You concealed in Your heart; I know that this was with You.
verses.10:14: If I sin, You keep watch over me, and You will not acquit me of my iniquity.
verses.10:15: If I am wicked, woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I cannot lift up my head, being sated with disgrace and beholding my affliction.
verses.10:16: Should my head lift itself up, You hunt me like a fierce lion, and again You display Your wondrous power against me.
verses.10:17: You renew Your witnesses against me and multiply Your indignation toward me; relays and a warring host are against me.
verses.10:18: Why then did You bring me forth from the womb? Would that I had breathed my last, and no eye had ever seen me!
verses.10:19: I would have been as though I had never existed, carried from the womb to the grave.
verses.10:20: Are not my days few? Cease then, and turn away from me, that I may take a little comfort,
verses.10:21: before I depart and do not return, to the land of darkness and the shadow of death,
verses.10:22: a land of deep gloom like thick darkness, of the shadow of death and without any order, where even the shining is like thick darkness.
verses.11:1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
verses.11:2: "Shall a multitude of words go unanswered, and shall a man full of talk be justified?
verses.11:3: Shall your empty boasts reduce men to silence? And when you mock, shall no one put you to shame?
verses.11:4: For you have said, 'My teaching is pure, and I am clean in Your sight.'
verses.11:5: But oh, that God would speak and open His lips against you,
verses.11:6: and declare to you the hidden depths of wisdom! For sound wisdom is manifold. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
verses.11:7: Can you search out the deep things of God? Can you attain to the utmost limit of the Almighty?
verses.11:8: It is as high as the heights of heaven—what can you do? Deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
verses.11:9: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
verses.11:10: If He passes by, imprisons, and summons an assembly, who can turn Him back?
verses.11:11: For He knows worthless men; He sees iniquity, and will He not take note of it?
verses.11:12: An empty-headed man will gain understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born a man.
verses.11:13: If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands toward Him,
verses.11:14: if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and do not let unrighteousness dwell in your tents—
verses.11:15: then surely you shall lift up your face without blemish; you shall be steadfast and shall not fear.
verses.11:16: For you shall forget your trouble; you shall remember it as waters that have passed away.
verses.11:17: And your life shall rise brighter than the noonday; even its darkness shall be like the morning.
verses.11:18: You shall be confident, because there is hope; you shall look around you and lie down in safety.
verses.11:19: You shall rest, and none shall make you afraid; and many shall seek your favor.
verses.11:20: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail; refuge shall perish from them, and their hope shall be the breathing out of the soul."
verses.12:2: "Truly you are the people, and wisdom shall die with you!
verses.12:3: Yet I also have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Indeed, who does not know such things as these?
verses.12:4: I have become a laughingstock to my friend—one who called upon God and He answered him; the righteous and blameless man is a laughingstock.
verses.12:5: In the mind of one who is at ease, a lamp is held in contempt; it awaits those whose feet are slipping.
verses.12:6: The tents of robbers prosper in peace, and those who provoke God dwell in security—even those who carry their god in their own hand.
verses.12:7: Yet ask now the beasts, and they shall instruct you; and the birds of the heavens, and they shall tell you;
verses.12:8: or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you; and the fish of the sea shall declare it to you.
verses.12:9: Who among all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has wrought this,
verses.12:10: in whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all human flesh?
verses.12:11: Does not the ear try words, just as the palate tastes its food?
verses.12:12: With the aged is wisdom, and in length of days is understanding.
verses.12:13: With Him reside wisdom and might; to Him belong counsel and understanding.
verses.12:14: Behold, He tears down, and it shall not be rebuilt; He shuts a man in, and it shall not be opened.
verses.12:15: Behold, He holds back the waters, and they dry up; He sends them forth, and they overturn the earth.
verses.12:16: With Him are strength and sound wisdom; both the one led astray and the one who leads astray belong to Him.
verses.12:17: He leads counselors away stripped, and turns judges into fools.
verses.12:18: He loosens the bonds of kings and binds a waistcloth about their loins.
verses.12:19: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty ones.
verses.12:20: He deprives the trusted of speech, and takes away the discernment of the elders.
verses.12:21: He pours out contempt upon nobles, and loosens the belt of the strong.
verses.12:22: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings forth the shadow of death into light.
verses.12:23: He makes nations great, and destroys them; He spreads nations abroad, and leads them away.
verses.12:24: He takes away the understanding of the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a pathless wasteland.
verses.12:25: They grope in darkness without light, and He makes them stagger like a drunken man."
verses.13:1: Behold, all this my eye has beheld; my ear has heard and comprehended it.
verses.13:2: As you know, so I also know; I do not fall short of you.
verses.13:3: Yet for my part, I would speak to the Almighty, and to reason with God is my desire.
verses.13:4: But as for you, you are plasterers of falsehood; physicians of no worth are all of you.
verses.13:5: Oh, that you would remain altogether silent, and that would become your wisdom!
verses.13:6: Hear now my plea, and give ear to the pleadings of my lips.
verses.13:7: Will you speak unrighteousness for God, and for Him will you speak deceit?
verses.13:8: Will you show partiality toward Him, or will you plead the cause of God?
verses.13:9: Would it go well if He should search you out? Or as one deceives a mortal man, will you deceive Him?
verses.13:10: Without fail He will rebuke you if in secret you show partiality.
verses.13:11: Does not His majesty fill you with terror, and His dread fall upon you?
verses.13:12: Your cherished maxims are proverbs of ashes; your bulwarks are bulwarks of clay.
verses.13:13: Keep silent before me, and I will speak; then let pass over me whatever may.
verses.13:14: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and place my life in the palm of my hand?
verses.13:15: Behold, though He should slay me, in Him I will hope; yet I will defend my ways before His face.
verses.13:16: He indeed shall be my salvation, for a godless man shall not come before Him.
verses.13:17: Hear my speech diligently, and let my declaration be in your ears.
verses.13:18: Behold now, I have set forth my case in order; I know that I shall be vindicated.
verses.13:19: Who is there to contend with me? For then I would be silent and breathe my last.
verses.13:20: Only do not do two things to me, and then I will not conceal myself from Your presence:
verses.13:21: Put Your hand far away from me, and do not let Your dread terrify me.
verses.13:22: Then call out, and I will answer; or let me speak, and return an answer to me.
verses.13:23: How many iniquities and sins are mine? Cause me to know my transgression and my sin.
verses.13:24: Why do You conceal Your face and reckon me as an enemy to Yourself?
verses.13:25: Will You terrify a windblown leaf, and will You pursue dry stubble?
verses.13:26: For You record bitter things against me, and cause me to inherit the iniquities of my youth.
verses.13:27: You place my feet in the stocks and keep watch over all my paths; You trace a boundary around the soles of my feet.
verses.13:28: And he wastes away like something rotten, like a garment that a moth has eaten.
verses.14:1: Man, born of a woman, is short of days and filled with turmoil.
verses.14:2: Like a blossom he comes forth and withers away; he flees like a shadow and does not abide.
verses.14:3: Yet even upon such a one do You open Your eyes, and do You bring me into judgment with Yourself?
verses.14:4: Who can bring forth the clean from the unclean? Not one.
verses.14:5: Since his days are decreed, and the number of his months is with You, You have set his bounds so that he cannot cross beyond.
verses.14:6: Turn Your gaze from him that he may rest, until he fulfills his day like a hired laborer.
verses.14:7: For a tree possesses hope: if it is hewn down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoot will not cease.
verses.14:8: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies in the dust,
verses.14:9: yet at the scent of water it will blossom and put forth boughs like a young plant.
verses.14:10: But a mighty man dies and is laid low; indeed, man breathes his last, and where is he?
verses.14:11: As waters vanish from a sea, and a river dwindles and dries up,
verses.14:12: so a man lies down and does not rise again; until the heavens are no more, they will not awaken, nor will they be stirred from their sleep.
verses.14:13: Oh, that You would conceal me in Sheol, that You would keep me hidden until Your wrath turns away, that You would set an appointed time for me and remember me!
verses.14:14: If a man dies, will he live once more? All the days of my appointed service I would wait, until my relief should come.
verses.14:15: You would call, and I myself would answer You; You would yearn for the work of Your hands.
verses.14:16: For now You count my steps; do You not keep watch over my sin?
verses.14:17: Sealed up in a pouch is my transgression, and You coat over my iniquity.
verses.14:18: Yet surely a falling mountain crumbles away, and a rock is removed from its place;
verses.14:19: waters wear down stones, and their torrents wash away the dust of the earth; thus You destroy the hope of mortal man.
verses.14:20: You overpower him forever, and he departs; You alter his countenance and send him away.
verses.14:21: His sons rise to honor, and he does not know it; they are brought low, and he takes no notice of them.
verses.14:22: Only his flesh upon him feels pain, and his soul within him mourns.
verses.15:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.15:2: "Should a wise man respond with knowledge of wind, and fill his belly with the east wind?
verses.15:3: Should he argue with talk that does not profit, or with words by which he can accomplish no good?
verses.15:4: Indeed, you make void reverence, and diminish meditation before God.
verses.15:5: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
verses.15:6: Your own mouth declares you guilty, and not I; yes, your own lips testify against you.
verses.15:7: Were you born as the first of mankind, or were you brought forth before the hills?
verses.15:8: Have you listened in the secret council of God, and do you limit wisdom to yourself?
verses.15:9: What do you know that we do not also know? What do you discern that is not with us?
verses.15:10: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, far greater in days than your father.
verses.15:11: Are the consolations of God too little for you, and the word spoken gently with you?
verses.15:12: Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,
verses.15:13: that you turn your spirit against God, and bring forth such words from your mouth?
verses.15:14: What is mortal man, that he should be pure, and he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
verses.15:15: Behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in His sight;
verses.15:16: how much less one who is detestable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!
verses.15:17: I will declare to you; listen to me, and what I have seen I will recount,
verses.15:18: what wise men have declared from their fathers, and have not concealed,
verses.15:19: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed through their midst:
verses.15:20: All his days the wicked man writhes in anguish, and numbered years are stored up for the ruthless.
verses.15:21: The sound of terrors is in his ears; in peace the destroyer comes upon him.
verses.15:22: He does not believe that he will return out of darkness, and he is awaited by the sword.
verses.15:23: He wanders about for bread, saying, 'Where is it?' He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.
verses.15:24: Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king poised for battle.
verses.15:25: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and acts defiantly against the Almighty,
verses.15:26: charging stubbornly against Him with the thick bosses of his shields;
verses.15:27: because he has covered his face with his fat, and gathered folds of fat upon his loins.
verses.15:28: He dwells in desolate cities, in houses no one inhabits, which are doomed to become heaps of ruins.
verses.15:29: He shall not grow rich, nor shall his wealth endure, nor shall their possessions spread over the earth.
verses.15:30: He shall not escape from darkness; the flame shall dry up his shoots, and he shall vanish by the breath of His mouth.
verses.15:31: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness shall be his recompense.
verses.15:32: Before his time it shall be paid in full, and his branch shall not be green.
verses.15:33: He shall drop his unripe grapes like a vine, and cast off his blossoms like an olive tree.
verses.15:34: For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
verses.15:35: They conceive trouble and bring forth iniquity, and their womb prepares deceit."
verses.16:2: "I have heard many things such as these; troublesome comforters are all of you!
verses.16:3: Is there any end to words of wind? Or what goads you that you answer?
verses.16:4: I also could speak as you do, if your soul were in the place of my soul; I could string words together against you, and shake my head at you.
verses.16:5: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips would bring relief.
verses.16:6: If I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I refrain, what departs from me?
verses.16:7: Surely now He has worn me out; You have made desolate all my company.
verses.16:8: You have shriveled me up, and it has become a witness; my leanness rises up against me, and testifies to my face.
verses.16:9: His wrath has torn me and harried me with hatred; He has gnashed at me with His teeth; my adversary sharpens His eyes against me.
verses.16:10: They have gaped at me with their mouths; in reproach they have struck my cheeks; together they band themselves against me.
verses.16:11: God delivers me over to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
verses.16:12: I was at ease, yet He shattered me; He seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces; He also set me up as His target.
verses.16:13: His archers encompass me; He splits open my kidneys and does not spare; He pours out my gall upon the ground.
verses.16:14: He breaks through me with breach upon breach; He charges against me like a mighty warrior.
verses.16:15: I have sewn sackcloth over my skin, and thrust my horn into the dust.
verses.16:16: My face is flushed from weeping, and upon my eyelids rests the shadow of death,
verses.16:17: although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
verses.16:18: O earth, do not cover my blood, and let there be no resting place for my outcry!
verses.16:19: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.
verses.16:20: My friends are my scorners; my eye pours out tears to God.
verses.16:21: Oh, that one might plead for a man with God, as a son of man pleads for his neighbor!
verses.16:22: For when a few years have come, I shall go the way from which I shall not return."
verses.17:1: My spirit is shattered, my days are extinguished; the graves await me.
verses.17:2: Surely mockers are with me, and my eye abides upon their bitter provocation.
verses.17:3: Lay down now a pledge, stand surety for me with Yourself; who is there who will strike hands with me?
verses.17:4: For You have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.
verses.17:5: He who informs against his friends for a share—even the eyes of his children shall fail.
verses.17:6: Yet He has set me as a byword of the peoples, and I have become one in whose face men spit.
verses.17:7: My eye has grown dim because of grief, and all my members are like a shadow.
verses.17:8: The upright are astonished at this, and the innocent stirs himself up against the godless.
verses.17:9: Yet the righteous holds fast to his way, and he who has clean hands increases in strength.
verses.17:10: But come back again, all of you, come now; for I shall not find one wise man among you.
verses.17:11: My days have passed by, my plans are torn apart, even the cherished desires of my heart.
verses.17:12: They turn night into day; light is near in the presence of darkness.
verses.17:13: If I look to Sheol as my house, and spread my bed in the darkness,
verses.17:14: if I cry to the pit, "You are my father," and to the worm, "My mother and my sister,"
verses.17:15: where then is my hope? As for my hope, who shall behold it?
verses.17:16: Will it go down to the bars of Sheol? Shall we rest together in the dust?
verses.18:1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.18:2: How long until you put an end to words? Consider, and afterward we will speak.
verses.18:3: Why are we counted as beasts, and regarded as senseless in your sight?
verses.18:4: You who tear yourself in your anger—shall the earth be forsaken for your sake, or shall the rock be moved from its place?
verses.18:5: Indeed, the light of the wicked shall be extinguished, and the flame of his fire shall not shine.
verses.18:6: The light grows dark in his tent, and his lamp above him is put out.
verses.18:7: His vigorous strides are straitened, and his own counsel casts him down.
verses.18:8: For he is thrust into a net by his own feet, and he walks upon a snare.
verses.18:9: A trap seizes him by the heel, and a snare lays fast hold upon him.
verses.18:10: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, and a trap for him upon the path.
verses.18:11: Terrors frighten him on every side and chase him at his heels.
verses.18:12: His strength is famished, and calamity stands ready at his side.
verses.18:13: It devours the parts of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
verses.18:14: He is torn from the tent in which he trusted, and brought before the king of terrors.
verses.18:15: What is none of his dwells in his tent; brimstone is scattered upon his habitation.
verses.18:16: His roots dry up beneath, and his branch withers above.
verses.18:17: His remembrance perishes from the earth, and he has no name upon the street.
verses.18:18: He is driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the inhabited world.
verses.18:19: He has neither offspring nor posterity among his people, nor any survivor where he dwelt.
verses.18:20: Those in the west are appalled at his day, and those in the east are seized with horror.
verses.18:21: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous, and this is the place of him who does not know God.
verses.19:2: How long will you torment my soul, and crush me with words?
verses.19:3: These ten times you have put me to shame; you are not ashamed to deal harshly with me.
verses.19:4: And even if indeed I have erred, my error remains with me.
verses.19:5: If indeed you magnify yourselves against me, and plead my reproach against me,
verses.19:6: know then that God has wronged me, and has cast His net around me.
verses.19:7: Behold, I cry out, "Violence!" yet I am not answered; I cry for help, yet there is no justice.
verses.19:8: He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and He has set darkness upon my paths.
verses.19:9: He has stripped my glory from me, and taken the crown from my head.
verses.19:10: He tears me down on every side, and I am gone; He has uprooted my hope like a tree.
verses.19:11: He has kindled His wrath against me, and He counts me as one of His adversaries.
verses.19:12: His troops come on together and build up their way against me; they encamp all around my tent.
verses.19:13: He has put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintances have become wholly estranged from me.
verses.19:14: My kinsfolk have failed me, and my close friends have forgotten me.
verses.19:15: Those who dwell in my house and my maidservants count me as a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their sight.
verses.19:16: I call to my servant, yet he does not answer; with my own mouth I must implore him.
verses.19:17: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to the children of my own body.
verses.19:18: Even young children despise me; when I rise up, they speak against me.
verses.19:19: All the men of my counsel abhor me, and those whom I loved have turned against me.
verses.19:20: My bone clings to my skin and to my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
verses.19:21: Have pity on me, have pity on me, O you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me!
verses.19:22: Why do you pursue me as God does, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
verses.19:23: Oh, that my words were written down! Oh, that they were inscribed in a book,
verses.19:24: with an iron pen and lead, carved into the rock forever!
verses.19:25: Yet as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last He shall rise upon the dust;
verses.19:26: and after my skin has been thus destroyed, yet from my flesh I shall behold God,
verses.19:27: Whom I shall behold for myself, and my own eyes shall see, and not another—my heart faints within my bosom!
verses.19:28: If you say, "How shall we pursue him?" since the root of the matter is found in me,
verses.19:29: fear the sword for yourselves, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment.
verses.20:1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
verses.20:2: "Therefore my anxious thoughts move me to reply, even because of the haste that is within me.
verses.20:3: I hear a reproof that brings me reproach, and a spirit from my understanding answers me.
verses.20:4: Do you know this from of old, ever since man was set upon the earth,
verses.20:5: that the exulting of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the godless is only for a moment?
verses.20:6: Though his loftiness ascends to the heavens, and his head reaches to the clouds,
verses.20:7: he shall perish forever like his own dung; those who saw him shall say, 'Where is he?'
verses.20:8: He shall fly away like a dream, and they shall not find him; he shall be driven away like a vision of the night.
verses.20:9: The eye that looked upon him shall see him no more, nor shall his place behold him any longer.
verses.20:10: His children shall seek the favor of the poor, and his own hands shall give back his wealth.
verses.20:11: His bones are full of his youthful vigor, yet it shall lie down with him in the dust.
verses.20:12: Though wickedness tastes sweet in his mouth, and he hides it beneath his tongue,
verses.20:13: though he spares it and will not let it go, keeping it still within his mouth,
verses.20:14: yet his food is turned in his stomach; it becomes the venom of asps within him.
verses.20:15: He swallows down riches, and he shall vomit them up again; God shall drive them out of his belly.
verses.20:16: He shall suck the poison of asps; the tongue of a viper shall slay him.
verses.20:17: He shall not look upon the streams, the rivers and brooks of honey and curds.
verses.20:18: He must give back what he toiled for, and shall not swallow it; according to the wealth of his gain, he shall not rejoice.
verses.20:19: For he has crushed and forsaken the poor; he has seized a house that he did not build.
verses.20:20: Because he knew no quietness within him, he shall not save anything that he prized.
verses.20:21: Nothing remained from his devouring; therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
verses.20:22: In the fullness of his abundance he shall be in distress; every hand of the afflicted shall come against him.
verses.20:23: To fill his belly, He shall send upon him the fierceness of His wrath, and shall rain it down on him as his food.
verses.20:24: He shall flee from the weapon of iron, yet a bow of bronze shall pierce him through.
verses.20:25: It is drawn forth and comes out of his back, and the glittering blade comes out of his gall; terrors fall upon him.
verses.20:26: Utter darkness is laid up for his treasures; a fire unfanned shall devour him, and it shall consume whatever remains in his tent.
verses.20:27: The heavens shall uncover his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him.
verses.20:28: The produce of his house shall depart, flowing away in the day of His wrath.
verses.20:29: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed to him by God."
verses.21:2: "Listen attentively to my words, and let this be your consolation.
verses.21:3: Bear with me that I may speak, and after I have spoken, keep on mocking.
verses.21:4: As for me, is my complaint against man? And why then should my spirit not be impatient?
verses.21:5: Look upon me and be appalled, and lay your hand over your mouth.
verses.21:6: Even when I think of it, I am dismayed, and trembling takes hold of my flesh.
verses.21:7: Why do the wicked live on, grow old, and also increase in power?
verses.21:8: Their offspring are established in their presence with them, and their descendants before their eyes.
verses.21:9: Their houses are safe from dread, and the rod of God is not upon them.
verses.21:10: His bull breeds without fail; his cow calves and does not miscarry.
verses.21:11: They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children dance about.
verses.21:12: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the flute.
verses.21:13: They finish their days in prosperity, and in an instant they go down to Sheol.
verses.21:14: Yet they say to God, 'Depart from us, for we do not desire the knowledge of Your ways.
verses.21:15: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him? And what profit do we have if we pray to Him?'
verses.21:16: Behold, their prosperity is not in their own hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
verses.21:17: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out, and their calamity comes upon them—the sorrows He allots in His anger?
verses.21:18: Are they like straw before the wind, and like chaff that a storm carries away?
verses.21:19: God lays up his iniquity for his children; let Him repay him himself, so that he may know it.
verses.21:20: Let his own eyes behold his ruin, and let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
verses.21:21: For what concern has he for his household after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
verses.21:22: Shall anyone teach God knowledge, seeing He judges those on high?
verses.21:23: One dies in the fullness of his vigor, wholly at ease and tranquil;
verses.21:24: his pails are full of milk, and the marrow of his bones is well moistened.
verses.21:25: And another dies in bitterness of soul, never having tasted good things.
verses.21:26: Together they lie down in the dust, and the worms cover over them.
verses.21:27: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the schemes by which you would wrong me.
verses.21:28: For you say, 'Where is the house of the nobleman, and where is the tent of the dwellings of the wicked?'
verses.21:29: Have you not asked those who travel the way, and do you not recognize their signs?
verses.21:30: that the wicked man is spared in the day of calamity, and they are led away in the day of wrath?
verses.21:31: Who declares his way to his face, and who repays him for what he has done?
verses.21:32: Yet he is borne to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
verses.21:33: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows after him, just as those before him are without number.
verses.21:34: How then can you comfort me with emptiness, since in your answers nothing remains but falsehood?"
verses.22:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.22:2: "Can a man be of benefit to God? Surely the prudent man is of benefit to himself.
verses.22:3: Is it a delight to the Almighty that you are righteous, or is it any gain that you make your ways perfect?
verses.22:4: Is it because of your reverence that He reproves you, and enters into judgment with you?
verses.22:5: Is not your wickedness abundant, with no end to your iniquities?
verses.22:6: For you have taken pledges from your brethren without cause, and stripped the garments from the naked.
verses.22:7: You have not given the weary water to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
verses.22:8: As for the man of might, the land belongs to him, and the honored man dwells in it.
verses.22:9: Widows you have sent away empty-handed, and the arms of the fatherless have been crushed.
verses.22:10: Therefore snares are all around you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
verses.22:11: or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of waters covers you.
verses.22:12: Is not God in the height of heaven? Behold the loftiest stars, how high they are!
verses.22:13: Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can He judge through the thick darkness?
verses.22:14: Clouds are a covering for Him, so that He does not see, and He walks about on the vault of heaven.'
verses.22:15: Will you keep to the ancient path that men of iniquity have trodden,
verses.22:16: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was swept away by a river,
verses.22:17: who said to God, 'Depart from us!' and, 'What can the Almighty do to them?'
verses.22:18: Yet He filled their houses with good things; but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
verses.22:19: The righteous see it and rejoice, and the innocent deride them:
verses.22:20: 'Surely our adversaries are cut off, and the fire has consumed their abundance!'
verses.22:21: Now be reconciled with Him and be at peace; in this way good shall come to you.
verses.22:22: Accept, please, instruction from His mouth, and set His words in your heart.
verses.22:23: If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, if you remove unrighteousness far from your tent.
verses.22:24: Lay your precious gold in the dust, and the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks;
verses.22:25: then the Almighty shall be your precious gold, and your choicest silver.
verses.22:26: For then you shall delight yourself in the Almighty, and lift up your countenance to God.
verses.22:27: You shall make supplication to Him, and He shall hear you, and you shall fulfill your vows.
verses.22:28: You shall also decree a matter, and it shall be established for you; and light shall shine upon your ways.
verses.22:29: When men are brought low, you shall say, 'There is lifting up!' for He saves him whose eyes are downcast.
verses.22:30: He shall deliver even one who is not innocent; indeed, he shall be delivered by the purity of your hands."
verses.23:2: "Even today my complaint is bitter; my hand lies heavy despite my groaning.
verses.23:3: Oh, that I knew where to find Him, that I might come to His dwelling place!
verses.23:4: I would lay out my case before Him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
verses.23:5: I would learn the words with which He would answer me, and understand what He would say to me.
verses.23:6: Would He contend with me in the greatness of His strength? No, surely He Himself would give heed to me.
verses.23:7: There an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
verses.23:8: Behold, I go forward, and He is not there; and backward, yet I do not perceive Him;
verses.23:9: on the left where He works, yet I cannot behold Him; He turns to the right, and I cannot see Him.
verses.23:10: Yet He knows the way that is with me; when He has tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
verses.23:11: My foot has held closely to His steps; I have kept His way and have not turned aside.
verses.23:12: I have not departed from the commandment of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my allotted portion.
verses.23:13: Yet He is unchangeable, and who can turn Him back? What His soul desires, He does.
verses.23:15: Therefore I am dismayed before His presence; when I consider it, I am in dread of Him.
verses.23:16: For God has made my heart faint, and the Almighty has terrified me;
verses.23:17: for I have not been silenced before the darkness, nor has He hidden the thick gloom from my face."
verses.24:1: "Why are times not laid up by the Almighty, and those who know Him do not behold His days?
verses.24:2: Men remove landmarks; they seize flocks by force and pasture them.
verses.24:3: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow's ox in pledge.
verses.24:4: They thrust the needy from the roadway; all the poor of the land hide themselves together.
verses.24:5: Behold, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go forth to their toil, seeking diligently for food; the desert plain yields them bread for their children.
verses.24:6: They reap his fodder in the field, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
verses.24:7: They spend the night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
verses.24:8: They are drenched by the mountain downpour, and for want of shelter they embrace the rock.
verses.24:9: Some snatch the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge against the poor.
verses.24:10: Naked they go about without clothing, and though hungry they carry the sheaves.
verses.24:11: Between their walls they press out oil; they tread the winepresses, yet they thirst.
verses.24:12: From out of the city men groan, and the soul of the wounded cries out; yet God does not impute wrong.
verses.24:13: They are among those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways, nor abide in its paths.
verses.24:14: At the break of light the murderer rises; he slays the poor and needy, and in the night he becomes like a thief.
verses.24:15: The eye of the adulterer also watches for the twilight, saying, 'No eye shall behold me,' and he sets a veil over his face.
verses.24:16: In the darkness they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
verses.24:17: For to all of them alike, morning is as the shadow of death, for each knows well the terrors of the shadow of death.
verses.24:18: Swift is he upon the face of the waters; their portion is accursed in the land; he does not turn toward the way of the vineyards.
verses.24:19: Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so does Sheol those who have sinned.
verses.24:20: The womb forgets him; the worm feasts sweetly on him; he shall be remembered no more, and unrighteousness shall be broken like a tree.
verses.24:21: He preys upon the barren woman who bears no child, and he does no good to the widow.
verses.24:22: Yet God drags away the mighty by His power; when He rises up, none is sure of life.
verses.24:23: He grants him security, and he leans upon it; yet His eyes are upon their ways.
verses.24:24: They are exalted for a little while, and then are no more; they are brought low, gathered in like all others, and cut off like the heads of grain.
verses.24:25: Now if it is not so, who will prove me a liar, and reduce my speech to nothing?"
verses.25:1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.25:2: "Dominion and dread rest with Him; He establishes peace in His lofty heights.
verses.25:3: Is there any count of His hosts? And upon whom does His light not arise?
verses.25:4: How then can mortal man be justified with God, and how can one born of a woman be pure?
verses.25:5: Behold, even the moon does not give brightness, and the stars are not pure in His sight;
verses.25:6: how much less mortal man, a maggot, and the son of man, a worm!"
verses.26:2: "How you have helped the one lacking strength, and delivered the arm without might!
verses.26:3: How you have counseled the one lacking wisdom, and made sound insight known in abundance!
verses.26:4: To whom have you uttered words, and whose breath has come forth from you?
verses.26:5: The shades of the dead tremble beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
verses.26:6: Sheol lies naked before Him, and Abaddon has no covering.
verses.26:7: He stretches out the north over the void; He suspends the earth upon nothing.
verses.26:8: He binds up the waters in His thick clouds, yet the cloud does not burst beneath them.
verses.26:9: He veils the face of the throne, and spreads His cloud over it.
verses.26:10: He has inscribed a circle upon the face of the waters, to the boundary of light and darkness.
verses.26:11: The pillars of the heavens shake, and are astounded at His rebuke.
verses.26:12: With His might He stilled the sea, and by His understanding He crushed Rahab.
verses.26:13: By His Spirit the heavens became fair; His hand pierced through the fleeing serpent.
verses.26:14: Behold, these are only the outer edges of His ways, and how faint a whisper is heard of Him! But who can comprehend the thunder of His mighty power?"
verses.27:1: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
verses.27:2: "As God lives, who has set aside my right, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul,
verses.27:3: as long as my breath remains within me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
verses.27:4: my lips shall not speak unrighteousness, nor shall my tongue utter deceit.
verses.27:5: Far be it from me that I should justify you! Until I die, I will not remove my integrity from myself.
verses.27:6: I hold fast to my righteousness and will not release it; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
verses.27:7: Let my enemy be as the wicked, and the one opposing me as the unrighteous.
verses.27:8: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his soul?
verses.27:9: Will God listen to his outcry when distress comes upon him?
verses.27:10: Will he find his delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
verses.27:11: I will instruct you concerning the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I will not hide.
verses.27:12: Behold, all of you yourselves have seen it; why then are you so utterly vain?
verses.27:13: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance that ruthless men receive from the Almighty:
verses.27:14: If his children increase, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not have their fill of bread.
verses.27:15: His survivors will be buried by death, and his widows will not weep.
verses.27:16: Though he piles up silver like dust and lays up apparel like clay,
verses.27:17: he may lay it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
verses.27:18: He builds his house like the moth, and like a shelter that a watchman fashions.
verses.27:19: He lies down rich, yet he will not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and he is gone.
verses.27:20: Terrors overtake him like waters; by night a whirlwind steals him away.
verses.27:21: The east wind lifts him up, and he departs; it hurls him out of his place.
verses.27:22: It hurls at him and shows no pity; he flees headlong from its power.
verses.27:23: It claps its hands at him, and hisses him out of his place."
verses.28:1: Truly there is a source for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.
verses.28:2: Iron is taken from the dust, and copper is poured forth from stone.
verses.28:3: Man sets a bound to darkness, and to every farthest limit he searches out the stone of gloom and the shadow of death.
verses.28:4: He breaks open a shaft away from where people dwell; forgotten by the foot, far from mankind they hang down and sway to and fro.
verses.28:5: As for the earth, bread comes forth from it, yet beneath it is overturned as by fire.
verses.28:6: Its stones are the place of sapphires, and it holds dust of gold.
verses.28:7: That path no bird of prey knows, nor has the falcon's eye caught sight of it.
verses.28:8: The proud beasts have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed along it.
verses.28:9: He puts forth his hand upon the flinty rock; he overturns mountains from their roots.
verses.28:10: He hews out channels through the rocks, and his eye beholds every precious thing.
verses.28:11: He binds up the streams from seeping, and brings what is hidden forth to light.
verses.28:12: Yet wisdom—where shall it be found? And where is the place of understanding?
verses.28:13: Mortal man does not know its worth, nor is it found in the land of the living.
verses.28:14: The deep says, "It is not within me," and the sea says, "It is not with me."
verses.28:15: Fine gold cannot be given in exchange for it, nor shall silver be weighed out as its price.
verses.28:16: It cannot be appraised with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or sapphire.
verses.28:17: Gold and glass cannot compare with it, nor can vessels of pure gold be its exchange.
verses.28:18: Coral and crystal shall not be mentioned, for the acquisition of wisdom surpasses rubies.
verses.28:19: The topaz of Cush cannot compare with it, nor can it be appraised with pure gold.
verses.28:20: Wisdom then—from where does it come? And where is the place of understanding?
verses.28:21: Indeed, it is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, and from the birds of the heavens it is concealed.
verses.28:22: Abaddon and Death say, "With our ears we have heard a report of it."
verses.28:23: God discerns the way to it, and He Himself knows its place.
verses.28:24: For He gazes to the ends of the earth, and sees beneath all the heavens.
verses.28:25: When He appointed weight for the wind, and meted out the waters by measure,
verses.28:26: when He made a decree for the rain, and a way for the thunderbolt,
verses.28:27: then He beheld it and declared it; He established it, and also searched it out.
verses.28:28: And He said to mankind, "Behold, the fear of the Lord—that is wisdom; and turning away from evil is understanding."
verses.29:1: Then Job once more took up his discourse and said:
verses.29:2: "Oh, that I were as in the months gone by, as in the days when God kept watch over me,
verses.29:3: when His lamp shone over my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness;
verses.29:4: as I was in the days of my prime, when the intimate counsel of God was over my tent,
verses.29:5: when the Almighty was still with me, and my children were round about me;
verses.29:6: when my footsteps were washed in cream, and the rock poured out streams of oil beside me!
verses.29:7: When I went forth to the gate up by the city, and prepared my seat in the open square,
verses.29:8: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the aged rose up and stood;
verses.29:9: princes restrained their words, and laid a hand upon their mouth;
verses.29:10: the voice of nobles was stilled, and their tongue clung to the roof of their mouth.
verses.29:11: When the ear heard, it called me blessed, and when the eye saw, it gave testimony for me,
verses.29:12: because I delivered the afflicted who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no helper.
verses.29:13: The blessing of the one who was perishing came upon me, and I made the heart of the widow sing for joy.
verses.29:14: Righteousness I put on, and it arrayed me; like a robe and a turban was my justice.
verses.29:15: I was eyes for the blind, and feet for the lame was I.
verses.29:16: I was a father to the needy, and the cause of one whom I did not know I searched out.
verses.29:17: I shattered the fangs of the unrighteous, and forced the prey from his teeth.
verses.29:18: Then I said, 'I shall expire in my nest, and like the sand I shall multiply my days;
verses.29:19: my root lies open to the waters, and the dew abides all night upon my bough;
verses.29:20: my glory remains fresh with me, and my bow is ever renewed in my hand.'
verses.29:21: To me they listened and waited, and remained silent for my counsel.
verses.29:22: After my word they did not speak again, and my speech dropped gently upon them.
verses.29:23: They waited for me as for rain, and opened their mouths wide as for the latter rain.
verses.29:24: When I smiled upon them, they did not believe it, and the light of my countenance they did not cast down.
verses.29:25: I chose their way and sat as chief; I dwelt like a king among the troops, as one who comforts the mourners."
verses.30:1: But now men younger than I in days laugh at me, whose fathers I disdained to put alongside the dogs of my flock.
verses.30:2: Indeed, of what use to me was the strength of their hands, men in whom mature vigor had perished?
verses.30:3: Gaunt from want and famine, they gnaw the dry earth by night, in waste and desolation.
verses.30:4: They pluck saltwort among the bushes, and the roots of the broom tree are their food.
verses.30:5: They are driven out from the midst of men; people shout after them as after a thief.
verses.30:6: They must dwell in the clefts of the ravines, in holes of the earth and among the crags.
verses.30:7: Among the bushes they bray; beneath the nettles they huddle together.
verses.30:8: Sons of fools, indeed sons of men without a name, they have been scourged out of the land.
verses.30:9: And now I have become their mocking song; yes, I am a byword to them.
verses.30:10: They abhor me, they keep far from me, and they do not hold back from spitting in my face.
verses.30:11: Because He has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me, they have cast off the bridle before my face.
verses.30:12: At my right hand the rabble rise up; they push away my feet, and build up against me their ways of destruction.
verses.30:13: They tear up my path; they hasten my ruin, though they have no helper.
verses.30:14: They come as through a wide breach; amid the ruin they roll on.
verses.30:15: Terrors are turned upon me; they pursue my honor like the wind, and my prosperity has passed away like a cloud.
verses.30:16: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction have seized me.
verses.30:17: The night pierces my bones within me, and my gnawing pains take no rest.
verses.30:18: By great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me tightly like the collar of my tunic.
verses.30:19: He has thrown me down into the mire, and I am likened to dust and ashes.
verses.30:20: I cry out to You, yet You do not answer me; I stand up, and You only look upon me.
verses.30:21: You have turned cruel to me; with the might of Your hand You oppose me.
verses.30:22: You lift me up to the wind and cause me to ride upon it; You melt away my substance.
verses.30:23: For I know that You will return me to death, to the house of assembly for all the living.
verses.30:24: Yet does not a man amid a heap of ruins stretch out his hand, or in his calamity therefore cry out for help?
verses.30:25: Did I not weep for him whose day was hard? Was not my soul grieved for the needy?
verses.30:26: Yet when I looked for good, evil came; and when I waited for light, thick darkness came.
verses.30:27: My inward parts boil and are not still; days of affliction have come to meet me.
verses.30:28: I go about in gloom, without the sun; I rise up in the assembly and cry for help.
verses.30:29: A brother I have become to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.
verses.30:30: My skin grows black and peels from me, and my bones burn with parching heat.
verses.30:31: My lyre has been turned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of those who weep.
verses.31:1: I made a covenant with my eyes; why then should I gaze upon a virgin?
verses.31:2: For what is the portion allotted by God from above, and the heritage of the Almighty from on high?
verses.31:3: Is there not calamity for the unjust, and misfortune for those who practice iniquity?
verses.31:4: Does not He Himself see my ways, and count every one of my steps?
verses.31:5: If I have walked with falsehood, or my foot has hastened toward deceit,
verses.31:6: let Him weigh me in just balances, that God may know my integrity.
verses.31:7: If my step has turned aside from the way, and my heart has walked after my eyes, or if any stain has clung to my hands,
verses.31:8: then let me sow and another eat, and let my harvest be uprooted.
verses.31:9: If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,
verses.31:10: then let my wife grind for another, and let other men bow down over her.
verses.31:11: For that would be a heinous wickedness; indeed, it would be an iniquity deserving of judgment.
verses.31:12: For that is a fire that consumes down to Abaddon, and would uproot all my increase.
verses.31:13: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or my maidservant when they contended with me,
verses.31:14: what then shall I do when God rises up? And when He calls to account, what shall I answer Him?
verses.31:15: Did not He who made me in the womb also make him? Did not the same One fashion us in the womb?
verses.31:16: If I have kept the poor from their desire, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
verses.31:17: or eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless did not eat of it—
verses.31:18: for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother's womb I have guided the widow—
verses.31:19: if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or the needy with no covering,
verses.31:20: if his loins have not blessed me, and he was not warmed by the fleece of my sheep;
verses.31:21: if I have raised my hand against the fatherless because I saw support for me in the gate,
verses.31:22: then let my shoulder fall from my shoulder blade, and let my arm be broken from its socket.
verses.31:23: For calamity from God was a dread to me, and before His majesty I could not endure.
verses.31:24: If I have made gold my hope, or said to fine gold, "You are my confidence";
verses.31:25: if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had acquired abundance;
verses.31:26: if I have gazed at the sun when it shone, or the moon advancing in splendor,
verses.31:27: so that my heart was secretly enticed, and my hand kissed my mouth,
verses.31:28: this also would be an iniquity deserving of judgment, for I would have denied God above.
verses.31:29: If I have rejoiced at the calamity of him who hated me, or exulted when evil overtook him—
verses.31:30: indeed, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—
verses.31:31: if the men of my tent have not said, "Who is there who has not been satisfied with his meat?"
verses.31:32: No sojourner had to lodge in the street; I opened my doors to the traveler.
verses.31:33: If I have covered my transgressions as Adam did, by hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
verses.31:34: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of the families terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go out of the door—
verses.31:35: Oh, that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature—let the Almighty answer me! And oh, that I had the indictment my adversary has written!
verses.31:36: Surely I would carry it upon my shoulder; I would bind it on myself like a crown.
verses.31:37: I would declare to Him the number of my steps; like a prince I would approach Him.
verses.31:38: If my own ground cries out against me, and all its furrows weep together;
verses.31:39: if I have eaten its yield without payment, or caused the life of its owners to expire,
verses.31:40: then let thorns spring up instead of wheat, and foul weeds instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
verses.32:1: Then these three men ceased from answering Job, for he was righteous in his own eyes.
verses.32:2: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled; against Job his wrath burned, because he justified himself rather than God.
verses.32:3: Against his three friends also his wrath burned, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
verses.32:4: Now Elihu had waited to speak with Job, because they were older in days than he.
verses.32:5: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, his wrath was kindled.
verses.32:6: So Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: "I am young in days, and you are aged; therefore I held back and was afraid to declare my opinion to you.
verses.32:7: I said, 'Days should speak, and a multitude of years should teach wisdom.'
verses.32:8: Yet there is a spirit in mortal man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
verses.32:9: It is not the great who are wise, nor do the aged understand justice.
verses.32:10: Therefore I say, 'Listen to me; I also will declare my opinion.'
verses.32:11: Behold, I waited for your words; I listened for your reasonings, while you searched out words.
verses.32:12: Indeed, I gave you my full attention, and behold, there was none among you who refuted Job, or who answered his words.
verses.32:13: Lest you say, 'We have found wisdom; God will vanquish him, not man.'
verses.32:14: Now he has not directed his words against me, and I will not reply to him with your speeches.
verses.32:15: They are dismayed and answer no more; words have departed from them.
verses.32:16: And shall I wait, because they do not speak, because they stand still and answer no more?
verses.32:17: I also will answer my part; I too will declare my opinion.
verses.32:18: For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.
verses.32:19: Behold, my belly is like wine that has not been opened; like new wineskins, it is about to burst.
verses.32:20: Let me speak, that I may find relief; I will open my lips and answer.
verses.32:21: Let me not show partiality to any man, nor give flattering titles to any mortal;
verses.32:22: for I do not know how to flatter, else my Maker would soon take me away."
verses.33:1: "But now, Job, hear my speech, I pray, and give ear to all my words.
verses.33:2: Behold now, I have opened my mouth; my tongue speaks in my palate.
verses.33:3: My sayings come from the uprightness of my heart, and my lips utter knowledge purely.
verses.33:4: The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives life to me.
verses.33:5: If you are able, answer me; set your case in order before me, and take your stand.
verses.33:6: Behold, before God I am just as you are; I also have been pinched out of clay.
verses.33:7: Behold, no dread of me shall terrify you, nor shall my pressure weigh heavy upon you.
verses.33:8: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the sound of your words, saying,
verses.33:9: 'I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no iniquity in me.
verses.33:10: Behold, He finds pretexts against me; He counts me as His enemy;
